These type of reports are required to be written and include sometimes ridiculous things but it's to prevent lawsuits from their investors and shareholders for the company not fully informing them of any possible risks. So, yes, cyptocurrencies are a possible competitor to Mastercard but that doesn't mean that they think they're going to be overthrown by Bitcoin tomorrow. It's just that, if they do get overthrown and lose money, the investors/stockholders could sue because they weren't made aware of this risk.

Same thing happened with Telsa a little while ago.
Smart analysis. Bitcoin is still far too small for these massive payment processors to take it seriously, but ti's good that they're paying attention.

If you want to know why anybody would want to pay more than a dollar for a pen and pencil ...

Sell me on it! I'm interested in hearing you convince me to get a fountain pen. I promise I won't be cynical or anything.

Well the main reasons are pretty much the same as the ones to get a better car, but these benefits come from 5-100 dollars rather than 5,000-40,000.

First of all, the feel of the pen while writing is much different. With a ballpoint you will have to press down hard to write at all, causing your hand to become strained and your handwriting to be less neat. Modern gel and rollerball pens solve some of these problems, but a fountain will still require the least amount of pressure, and with a finely tuned pen you might not even need to press down at all, and the pen will not have friction going across the page. Some people want the friction on the page so they have more control, so another nice thing about fountain pens is that you can control that and change the smoothness and wetness to your desire (but it may require micromesh). At the same time you can choose how wide you want your pen to write, or you could do calligraphy with a stub or italic nib or even flex some nibs for a different type of calligraphy. Not only do you choose the size of the writing, you can choose from almost unlimited colors, and inks that have different properties like water resistance, pigments such as chlorophyll(the maker of this ink stopped making that ink though so very little is left), scents, and even the ability to glow in the dark. The materials are also not just cheap plastic, if you name a material it has probably been made into a pen before or could be even cheese plastic you could make at home and eat (paneer/casein). The materials have different colors or may feel differently in the hand like something other than lifeless plastic, as well as having some heft. The ways to refill the pen are also more interesting; some have a piston inside the pen that you work by twisting the back, some have a mini and removable version that fits inside the barrel, some have little plastic tubes that attach to the pen, some even absorb ink magically. Another allure of fountain pens (and nice pens) is the feel that you have a pen made to last, and one that could out last you at that (I own a pen from the 20's/30's), or the patronage of an artist.
Because they write far better than any other pen you've written with. No doubt.

Your hand writing is about more than how you shape the letters. Writing with a fountain pens makes the speed, pressure, angle, even ink type all part of your handwriting and all decisions that were taken by the writer. A nib will bend and flex (even the rigid ones) to fit how you write so it is truly unique to you. That's what keeps me enjoying my fountain pens
